sop-from-memo.output:
Water Heater Swap — Maple & Sons Plumbing

You will need

- Main water shutoff valve (outside or basement)
- Electrical breaker for water heater
- Garden hose from van
- Floor drain access
- New flexible water lines (one pair per job)
- New water heater unit
- Camera or phone for photo documentation

Steps

1. Shut off water at the main shutoff valve. Do not rely on the local shutoff valve alone.

2. Turn off the electrical breaker for the water heater at the panel.

3. Attach the garden hose to the drain valve and run it to the floor drain. Open the drain valve fully and let the tank empty completely.

4. Disconnect both water supply lines and the power connections from the old unit.

5. Remove the old water heater from its location and position the new unit in place.

6. Install new flexible water lines from the new unit to the main supply and return — use new lines every time, regardless of how the old lines appear.

7. Check if there is a check valve on the main shutoff. If yes, ASK OWNER about expansion tank installation or adjustment before filling.

8. Close the drain valve. Open the main shutoff to fill the new tank.

9. Bleed air from the system by opening the closest hot water faucet in the building. Run it until water flows without sputtering.

10. Restore power to the water heater breaker.

11. Wait 20 minutes. Inspect all connection points and the base of the unit for leaks.

12. Take a photo of the completed installation and file it with the job record.

Done looks like

Tank full and holding pressure. Hot water flows at the nearest faucet. No water dripping from any connection. Electrical power restored and breaker in ON position. Photo taken and filed.

Common mistakes

1. Powering on before bleeding air — check that you heard water flowing (not air) at the faucet and waited at least 20 minutes after filling before restoring breaker.

2. Forgetting the expansion tank when a check valve is present on the main — ask the owner on site if there is a check valve, and confirm what to do with the expansion tank before you start.

3. Checking for leaks too soon — wait the full 20 minutes after power is on; a slow leak may not show up in 2 minutes.

Service Plumber, Marietta GA and north side. Mon–Fri 7am to 4pm, weekend rotation one in three. Van provided. $28–34/hour based on skill.

You run calls alone by month two. We do residential work — water heaters, fixtures, drains, gas lines. You'll diagnose, quote, and close jobs without a supervisor on site. Some days are straightforward; some are in crawl spaces or attics. You need to solder, sweat fittings, read plans, and talk to homeowners straight.

We're looking for someone who can show up, problem-solve, and own the work. If you've done this before and can prove it, send us three things: your name, phone, and the name of a plumber or manager who's watched you solder and work alone on a real job. No resumes needed. 1. Tell us about a time you soldered or sweated a copper joint on a live job. What was the fitting, and who watched you do it?

2. Have you worked service calls alone, or have you always had someone else on site? If alone, how long have you been doing that?

3. We work Saturdays and Sundays one week in three. Can you commit to that rotation, or do you need weekends off?
